fields.h1: Build a Ladder Inspection Form Your Crews Fill Out on Site
fields.hero_description: Build a ladder inspection form that logs each check by ladder ID and takes any ladder that fails out of service.
fields.features_subheading: Describe your ladders and who inspects them. Emergent builds the form, the ladder register, and the email sent when a ladder fails.
fields.feature_1:
Every ladder picked by its ID

Give every ladder a number once, such as L-07 or EX-12, and the worker picks it from a list on the form. Each check is saved against that ladder with a name and a time.
fields.feature_2:
Questions that match the ladder type

Each check is a short pass or fail list. A step ladder asks about the spreaders and the locks, while an extension ladder asks about the rope, the pulley, and the rung locks.
fields.feature_3:
One failed item, ladder out of service

A failed check changes the ladder's status to Do not use in the register. The safety manager gets an email naming the ladder and the item that failed, with a link to the record.
fields.feature_4:
A photo whenever an item fails

Add a photo field that opens only when an answer is Fail. The worker photographs the crack or the bent rung from the form, and the picture stays attached to that ladder's history.
fields.feature_5:
Inspections signed by the inspector

The inspector signs the monthly inspection on a phone or tablet once the last ladder is checked. The signature, the date, and every pass or fail answer are saved together.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take to your own servers

On paid plans, export the full codebase to your GitHub repository and host it anywhere. Teams that run their own safety system can fold the ladder records into it there.

fields.tab_content_1:
With all 8 checks passed, L-07 is in use by 7 AM

Tollworth Hardware checks each step ladder before its first climb of the shift. At 6:52 AM, stocker Stavros Ikonomou picks L-07 on his phone and answers 8 pass or fail questions on the feet, steps, spreaders, and locks. All 8 pass, the check is saved under L-07, and the ladder is in use when the store opens at 7 AM.
fields.tab_content_2:
After one cracked rail, EX-12 is out of service

Rafael Gallardo sets up 28-foot extension ladder EX-12 on a Hartsgrove Roofing job and checks it before he climbs. He marks the left side rail Fail for a crack near the base and adds a photo. The form sets EX-12 to Do not use and emails safety manager Tereza Folau the ladder, the failed item, and a link to the photo.
fields.tab_content_3:
Each month, 14 van ladders and one signature

Once a month, Yolanda Hennessy inspects the 14 ladders that ride on Velloran Electric's service vans, van by van in the yard. Of the 14, 13 pass, and ladder V-09 goes for repair with a bent rung lock. When the last ladder is done, she signs the inspection on her tablet, and it is filed with all 14 results.
fields.tab_content_4:
Which of 32 ladders are out of service or overdue

Ottercreek Property Management owns 32 ladders across 4 buildings, and the register shows each one with its status and next monthly inspection. Two are marked Do not use. Three inspections are overdue, the oldest at Harbor Court by 9 days. A repaired ladder stays at Do not use until it passes a new inspection.

faq_plan.q: What is a ladder inspection form?
How do I create a ladder inspection form?

plan.angle: The results for this query are printable ladder checklists (PDF, Word, Etsy downloads) and university or state OSHA checklists that list what to look at. None shows what happens after a box is ticked: which ladder was checked, who checked it, what happens to a ladder that fails, and how a safety manager sees which ladders are due. This page shows a working ladder inspection form for four moments (the pre-shift check, a failed ladder, the periodic inspection by a competent person, the ladder register), with every inspection saved to a database the company owns. OSHA wording is quoted from the two ladder standards; no safety guarantees and no compliance claims.
tab_stories: At Tollworth Hardware, stocker Stavros Ikonomou picks step ladder L-07 on his phone before his 7 AM shift, answers 8 checks, all pass, and the check is logged with his name and the time.

At Hartsgrove Roofing, crew lead Rafael Gallardo finds a cracked side rail on 28-foot extension ladder EX-12; one failed check sets the ladder to Do not use and emails safety manager Tereza Folau with a link to the photo.
At Velloran Electric, Yolanda Hennessy inspects the 14 ladders on the company's vans each month, 13 pass, 1 is sent for repair, and she signs the inspection when the last ladder is done.

At Ottercreek Property Management, the ladder register lists 32 ladders across 4 buildings: 2 are out of service and 3 monthly inspections are overdue, and a repaired ladder returns to service only after it passes a new inspection.

claims_to_source: OSHA 1910.23(b)(9): ladders are inspected before initial use in each work shift, and more frequently as necessary, to identify visible defects
OSHA 1910.23(b)(10): any ladder with structural or other defects is immediately tagged Dangerous: Do Not Use or similar and removed from service until repaired or replaced
OSHA 1926.1053(b)(15): in construction, ladders are inspected by a competent person for visible defects on a periodic basis and after any occurrence that could affect their safe use
